title: Careful With What Is Not Ours

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If anyone grazes their livestock in a field or vineyard and lets them stray and they graze in another person's field, they must make restitution from the best of their own field or vineyard." - Exodus 22:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the harm is not deliberate theft but plain carelessness — letting your animals wander onto a neighbour's field and eat his crop. And yet God still requires restitution, and not from your leftovers but from the best of your own field. Negligence that damages another person is not excused simply because you did not mean it. You still make it right, and generously.

This searches our hearts. So much of the harm we cause others comes not from malice but from carelessness — the commitment we forgot, the mess we left for someone else, the way our choices spilled over onto people we never intended to affect. God calls us to a thoughtful love that watches its own boundaries and takes responsibility when we cross them.

Notice too the generosity built in: repay from your best. God's people are not to make grudging, bare-minimum repairs, but to restore wholeheartedly. This reflects the very generosity of God toward us. He did not give us the leftovers of heaven; He gave His best, His own Son (Rom 8:32). A heart shaped by that kind of grace becomes generous in making things right, quick to own its carelessness and eager to repair it well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Where has my carelessness spilled over and harmed someone else?
Do I make repairs grudgingly, or generously from my best?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You gave me Your very best in Christ. Make me watchful over my own carelessness and generous in setting things right, reflecting the grace You have shown me. Amen.
